<description>
IPC clients can hold block templates indefinitely, keeping transactions alive after they leave the mempool. This adds `getMemoryLoad()` to estimate the memory held on behalf of all mining clients, as discussed in bitcoin/bitcoin#33899. It does not impose a limit.

The estimate includes each tracked template's vectors and the transactions it references that are no longer in the mempool. Transaction objects shared by multiple templates are counted once. Dummy coinbase transactions and the template cached by the `getblocktemplate` RPC are excluded.

`BlockTemplateManager` tracks templates through weak references, so the registry does not prolong their lifetime. Templates unregister when destroyed, including when IPC cleanup happens after shutdown has reset the manager. Clients can reduce the reported memory load by releasing stale templates or explicitly calling `destroy()`.

The result is an estimate: the mempool can change during calculation, and eviction followed by re-entry as a different transaction object can cause undercounting.

Example client usage: [stratum-mining/sv2-tp#63](https://github.com/stratum-mining/sv2-tp/pull/63).

Commits:

- `refactor: pass block template by reference to WaitAndCreateNewBlock`
- `refactor: share ownership of BlockTemplateManager`
- `mining: track block templates held by IPC clients`
- `mining: add GetTemplateMemoryUsage()`
- `ipc: add getMemoryLoad()`
- `test: check template memory accounting invariants`
</description>
